Area.evidence_source: The coming-out process (defined in most L/B/G literature as disclosure of one's nonexclusive heterosexuality to self and/or others) has been highlighted as a particularly vulnerable period for suicidal behaviour (Bagley & Ramsay, 1997; Friedman & Downey, 1994; Proctor & Groze, 1994; Remafedi et al., 1991; Schneider et al., 1989). One of the reasons for such vulnerability is likely to be the inevitable clash with a heterosexist society. Heterosexism refers to the privileging and institutionalisation of of heterosexuality and the assumption that everyone is heterosexual (Adams, 1996; Cruickshank, 1992; Herek, 1996; Logan, 1996). Heterosexism may place L/B/G people at greater risk of negative psychological outcomes; for not only must such persons endure the "everyday" stresses common to straight populations, but they may also face discrimination that is often enshrined in common law (e.g., sodomy laws, lack of de-facto partner rights).
